statement.p: Find the critical point of the function f(x,y)=4e^{x}-xe^{y}.

Use the Second Derivative Test to determine whether it is
a local minimum
a saddle point
a local maximum
test fails

static.solution:
f(x,y)=4e^{x}-xe^{y} equal to zero and solve f_x(x,y)=4e^{x}-e^{y}=0 f_y(x,y)=-xe^{y}=0 Since e^y\ne 0, the second equation gives x=0. Substituting in the first equation, we get: 4 e^0-1 e^y=0 \Rightarrow y=\ln (4/1)=1.38629
Now we compute the Discriminant. We find the second-order partials: f_{xx}(x,y)=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(4e^{x}-e^{y}\right)=4e^{x} f_{yy}(x,y)=\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(-xe^{y}\right)=-xe^{y} f_{xy}(x,y)=\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(4e^{x}-e^{y}\right)=-e^{y} The discriminant is thus D(x,y)=f_{xx}f_{yy}-f_{xy}^2=-\left(4xe^{x+y}+e^{2y}\right)
Applying the Second Derivative Test we have D(0,1.38629)=-16\lt 0 We conclude that f(0,1.38629) is a saddle point.
